tasks.short: Plan and lead balanced learning activities

steps.what: Choose learning goals, available materials and activity constraints
Draft balanced activities with instruction, demonstration and investigation time

loop.purpose: Draft alternative activity sequences against teacher-selected goals
loop.output: timed activity plan with materials and goal references
loop.check: Teacher verifies activities actually teach the named goals, materials are safe and available, and timing permits questioning
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; teacher writes unsuitable sections
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed activity catalogue remains first choice; generating a new sequence requires language and pedagogical variation

steps.what: Adapt and conduct activities as students observe, question and investigate

tasks.design: Use a native {LMS} activity assistant or approved {DOCS} drafting tool with a teacher-written brief. The teacher checks the final plan before leading the class and continues to change activities during instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing varied activity sequences takes preparation time even when goals are known.
tasks.enabler_now: Goal-conditioned activity drafting is available in named teaching products.
tasks.still_hard: The teacher must judge safety, readiness and live classroom responses.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion and make space for productive questions.

ambition.what: Compare two feasible activities before choosing a lesson sequence.

tasks.altitude: The teacher gains faster draft alternatives, with unchanged authority over lesson delivery.

reach.task: Compare activity alignment with curriculum goals
reach.learn: Map each activity to explicit learning goals

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts classroom activities from lesson goals.
The digest reports a primary-school trial of Aila with lower preparation time and limited lesson coverage; that does not establish this task estimate.

assumptions: The teacher supplies goal codes, duration, materials and broad class constraints in the activity brief; missing details are clarified manually before drafting.
Test the native activity catalogue and assistant before building anything; use only approved tools and omit pupil-identifying information.
Only plan drafting changes; choosing goals and conducting instruction retain their full baseline time.
unknowns: Which approved assistant and activity library the school already uses
research_questions: Across ten lessons, how much drafting time remains after checking educational fit and safety?

already_counted.description: Check generated activities against goals and classroom constraints

incremental.description: Maintain reusable briefs and record unsuitable drafts

approvals.approved_version: Teacher accepts the exact final activity-plan revision before delivery; edits require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100, R=10+7.5+75=92.5, gross=7.5%; minus 1 focal upkeep gives 6.5% net. Low: existing catalogue is quicker or drafts fail checks. High: suitable drafts consistently halve the 15% planning slice; classroom time stays unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read books with classes and small groups

steps.what: Select books and prepare the class or small group
Read books aloud and respond to students during shared reading

tasks.design: Keep shared reading with the teacher, using the selected physical or locally approved digital book. No software replacement is proposed for the teacher’s pacing, expression or response to children.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task is a live educational interaction rather than document production.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technical capability justifies removing teacher reading time here.
tasks.still_hard: Responding sensitively to questions and differing comprehension.
tasks.human_edge: Make the story meaningful through expression and interaction.
tasks.altitude: Reading responsibility and time remain with the teacher.

evidence.claim: Teacher-led read-aloud work depends on live pacing and response to students; replacing narration does not preserve the same activity.

assumptions: The boundary includes selecting the book and reading it with pupils, excluding separate lesson-material production.
No new application or data feed is introduced, so incremental maintenance is zero.
unknowns: Which books and accessibility formats pupils need
research_questions: Would existing accessible book formats help participation without reducing shared reading?

incremental.description: No new software or process; existing work remains in the baseline

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100. Both selection and live reading retain their time; no incremental system work or savings is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe students’ performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Evaluate observations against learning goals and identify concerns
Record evaluations and concerns in the pupil record

tasks.design: Configure a concise observation form in {OTHER}, the pupil record system, with existing goals available for selection. The teacher supplies all observations and evaluations; the form only avoids repeated record headers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated pupil identifiers and dates can add record-entry effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil-record products already support learning-goal tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing observed behavior from interpretation and knowing when to seek support.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the child in context without automated diagnostic or emotion labels.
tasks.altitude: The teacher records observations more directly; evaluative responsibility remains unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss support needs based on documented observations

evidence.claim: ParnasSys provides pupil records and learning-goal tracking.
Reducing repeated header entry with a configured form is a proposed implementation, not demonstrated by the digest.

assumptions: The existing pupil system supplies pupil_id, current teacher access, observation date and goal catalogue; teacher enters observation text and assessment. Missing or ambiguous pupil identity blocks saving until manually resolved.
Test native forms first; no health inference, outcome scoring, emotion detection or additional data sharing is introduced.
This task covers brief assessment recording, not duplicate report-writing or parent correspondence.
unknowns: Whether current forms already prefill these fields
Which access permissions govern sensitive observations
research_questions: Does a shorter form reduce duplicate entry without losing observational detail?

already_counted.description: Enter and verify the pupil assessment record

incremental.description: Review form fields when goals change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=65+25+8=98; gross=2%, less 0.5 focal maintenance gives 1.5% net. Low: headers already prefill. High: modest repeated-entry reduction is real; observation and evaluation remain fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer about behavioral and academic problems

steps.what: Review relevant observations before discussing students’ behavioral and academic problems
Confer with parents, guardians and school colleagues to agree support actions
Record agreed actions and responsibilities after the discussion

tasks.design: Use the existing {OTHER} pupil record for preparation and agreed action notes. Keep the conversation, interpretation and agreement with the people involved; no recording or generated account is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficulty is building a shared understanding rather than producing a meeting transcript.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing pupil records support preparation; the digest does not establish a better mechanism for this conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Disagreement, sensitive context and workable commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and hear explanations that are absent from records.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains the same convening and support responsibilities.

reach.learn: Use clear ownership and review dates

evidence.claim: ParnasSys includes pupil records and a parent application; this does not demonstrate automated conflict resolution.

assumptions: Existing access-controlled records are available; gaps in the relevant observations are clarified with their authors.
Parent and colleague participation remains outside focal teacher labour, unchanged and not counted as savings.
No new process or integration is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; meeting scheduling and report generation are outside this task.
unknowns: Who may access each support record
Which participants and interpreters are needed
research_questions: Do action records already identify an owner and review date for each commitment?

incremental.description: No new software or process; existing work remains in the baseline

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+70+10=100. Preparation, conversation and recording retain their existing effort; no new maintenance or labour transfer is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher can draft learning activities faster while retaining direct instruction, assessment and family conversations.
reach: Compare curriculum alignment with an instructional coordinator
Use observation records to discuss support with specialist staff
skills_to_grow: Check generated activities for educational fit and safety
role.ambitious_version: Use saved preparation time to offer more considered activity choices without automating pupil evaluation.

job.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
